result.verdict_statement: FAIL. test/letflow/service_catalog_test.exs:724, describe "REQ-192 list_all/1 <-> list_for_tenant/2: SCA:/SC: cursor cross-endpoint isolation (INV-9)", test "SCA: is not merely a longer match of SC: -- an SC:-prefixed cursor never accidentally satisfies list_all/1's own prefix check" is not a runnable test -- it crashes with `** (FunctionClauseError) no function clause matching in Base.url_decode64!/2` on every run (confirmed deterministic, both in the full two-file run and in isolation via `mix test test/letflow/service_catalog_test.exs:724`), because it calls `register!(%{scope: :global})` exactly once and then calls `ServiceCatalog.list_for_tenant(%{page_size: 1}, tenant.id)` with page_size: 1 against that single row -- with only one row and page_size 1, that single row IS the full result set, so next_cursor is nil per this exact codebase's own pagination semantics (the sibling pagination-correctness describe block two sections below asserts precisely this: 'next_cursor is nil on the first page when the full result set fits within page_size'). `sc_cursor` is therefore `nil`, and `Base.url_decode64!(nil, padding: false)` has no matching function clause. This is not a design/reasoning gap in the test's intent (the regression it guards against -- SCA:/SC: prefix-relationship confusion -- is a legitimate, real concern per the rationale) -- it is a fixture-sizing bug: the test needs at least 2 registered rows with page_size: 1 (or any page_size less than the row count) to force a non-nil cursor, exactly as the working sibling tests in the same describe block do (they each register 2 rows before minting a cursor).
